value: Mid-fusion architecture built on the Phi-4-Reasoning language model backbone and SigLIP-2 vision encoder; the vision encoder converts images into visual tokens, which are projected into the language model's embedding space and injected into the pretrained language model, leveraging both pretrained components while keeping training and inference costs manageable. Dynamic resolution vision encoder with up to 3,600 visual tokens for high-resolution understanding (GUI grounding, fine-grained document analysis). Bidirectional attention is applied within images (intra-image) to improve spatial reasoning without the overfitting risks of broader bidirectional schemes. 15B parameters.

value: Mid-fusion architecture combining the Phi-4-Reasoning backbone and SigLIP-2 vision encoder, chosen to leverage both pretrained components while keeping training and inference costs manageable. A dynamic resolution vision encoder (up to 3,600 visual tokens) enables high-resolution understanding for GUI grounding and document analysis. Bidirectional attention is applied only within images to improve spatial reasoning without the overfitting risks of broader bidirectional schemes. A single model handles both reasoning and non-reasoning modes rather than separate models.
quote: This approach leverages the strengths of both pretrained components while keeping training and inference costs manageable. [...] The model employs a dynamic resolution vision encoder with up to 3,600 visual tokens, enabling high-resolution image understanding critical for tasks such as GUI grounding and fine-grained document analysis. [...] Bidirectional attention is applied within images (intra-image) to improve spatial reasoning without the overfitting risks observed with broader bidirectional schemes. [...] Rather than training separate models for each mode, the model operates as a single system that can invoke extended chain-of-thought reasoning (using `<think>...</think>` blocks) for tasks like mathematical and scientific reasoning, or default to direct inference (tagged with `<nothink>`) for perception-focused tasks such as captioning, object detection, and grounding.
